rationale: B wins because it treats the pilot fact as a separate, gated utility-operations story instead of laundering the same evidence into a sweeping contrarian thesis. Its line, "Without a named utility this angle does not exist yet," is exactly the adult supervision this update needs. A has good bones, but "Rooftop and community solar were sold as an easy win" imports an unsupported premise and even adds rooftop solar, which Verdano never gave us.
gaps_in_A: "Rooftop and community solar were sold as an easy win" adds rooftop solar and a public-perception claim that are not in the update.
"An ex-Tesla Energy engineer and an ex-NREL researcher" states roles the update does not provide; the proof section later admits those roles still need confirmation.
"Three utilities already trust Verdano's AI" is refused as a duplicate, but a named-utility pilot story is a real bottom-rung trade angle if one customer will go on record.
"find-journalists once you pick between the trend and contrarian angles" is premature for those two angles; the named-utility proof gap is the real gate.
gaps_in_B: "local solar output that the wires were not sized for" invents a technical premise beyond the supplied "grid strain" fact.
"someone who shipped commercial energy products at Tesla Energy" and "someone who did the underlying grid research" invent founder work histories not in the update.
"It is the only angle whose proof you already hold" overstates the founder-profile readiness; roles, teams, dates, and projects still need confirmation.
"a letter of intent" muddies the update's cleaner fact that the three utilities are paying customers, though asking for contract structure is still fair.
